main_topics.reason: The user described severe nausea after the weekly dose and returned to ways to make it manageable.
The user opened by asking whether to quit, then explored alternatives because the medicine helps their hands.
The user asked whether taking folic acid on the methotrexate day was a problem and agreed to change the timing.
The user asked whether injections could help and discussed feeling scared to inject themselves.
The user asked whether an anti-nausea medicine could be taken safely with methotrexate.
The user asked what to tell the doctor so they would remember the options, and accepted a suggested note.

output.summary: The user considered stopping weekly methotrexate because of severe nausea after dosing, despite improved hand symptoms, and asked about alternatives including folic acid timing, dose splitting, injections, and anti-nausea medication. The assistant outlined options and helped prepare questions for the rheumatology visit; the user said they felt much better, planned to move folic acid to Sunday and take the tablets with food, and accepted continuing methotrexate as prescribed until an appointment in about two weeks.
